title: Short title, extent and commencement
verbatim_text: (1) This Ordinance may be called the Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance, 2001. (2) It extends to the whole of Pakistan. (3) It shall come into force at once.

title: Definitions
verbatim_text: In this Ordinance, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context: (a) 'Banking Court' means a Court established under section 4; (c) 'customer' means a person to whom finance has been extended by a financial institution; (d) 'finance' includes an accommodation or facility provided on the basis of participation in profit and loss, mark-up, lease, hire-purchase, or loan; (e) 'financial institution' means any bank or development finance institution; (f) 'obligation' includes any agreement, undertaking or liability to pay money or repay finance.

title: Duty of a customer
verbatim_text: (1) It shall be the duty of a customer to fulfil all his obligations to the financial institution as per terms agreed upon.

title: Establishment of Banking Court
verbatim_text: (1) The Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, establish as many Banking Courts as it considers necessary to exercise jurisdiction under this Ordinance.

title: Powers of Banking Courts
verbatim_text: (1) Subject to the provisions of this Ordinance, a Banking Court shall in the exercise of its civil jurisdiction have all the powers vested in a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

title: Suit for recovery of written off finances
verbatim_text: (1) Where any finance has been written off by a financial institution, a suit for recovery may be instituted under this section within the prescribed period.

title: Procedure of Banking Court
verbatim_text:
(1) Where a customer or a financial institution commits a default in fulfillment of any obligation, the financial institution or, as the case may be, the customer, may institute a suit in the Banking Court by presenting a plaint which shall be verified on oath.
(2) The plaint shall be supported by a statement of account verified on oath in terms of the Bankers' Books Evidence Act, 1891.

title: Leave to defend
verbatim_text:
(1) The defendant shall not be entitled to defend the suit unless he applies for and obtains leave from the Banking Court as hereinafter provided.
(2) The application for leave to defend shall be filed within thirty days of the date of first service by any of the prescribed modes.
(3) The application for leave to defend shall be in the form of a written statement verified on oath and shall state the specific amount of finance availed, repayments made, and the exact amount disputed.
(4) If the defendant fails to file an application for leave to defend within thirty days, the Banking Court shall pass a decree forthwith.

title: Judgment on refusal to grant leave
verbatim_text: Where the Banking Court refuses to grant leave to defend or the defendant fails to comply with the condition on which leave was granted, the Court shall forthwith pass a decree in favor of the plaintiff.

title: Interim Decree
verbatim_text: (1) If the Banking Court is of the opinion that the dispute between the parties pertains only to a part of the claim, it shall immediately pass an interim decree in respect of that part of the claim which is admitted or indisputable.

title: Power to set aside ex-parte decree
verbatim_text: In any case in which a decree is passed against a defendant who failed to apply for leave to defend, the Banking Court may set aside the decree on an application filed within twenty-one days if special reasons are shown.

title: Disposal of suit
verbatim_text: A suit in the Banking Court shall be disposed of expeditiously and preferably within ninety days from the date of filing of the plaint.

title: Sale of mortgaged property without intervention of Court
verbatim_text:
(1) In this section, 'mortgaged property' means any immoveable property mortgaged by a customer or mortgagor in favour of a financial institution as security for finance.
(2) Where a customer commits default, the financial institution may send three notices demanding payment and upon non-compliance, proceed to sell the mortgaged property by public auction without intervention of court.

title: Attachment before judgment
verbatim_text: The Banking Court may, on application of the financial institution, attach the properties of the defendant before judgment if satisfied that the defendant is about to dispose of or remove property.

title: Arrest before judgment
verbatim_text: The Banking Court may issue a warrant of arrest against a defendant if satisfied that he is about to abscond or leave the local limits of the Court.

title: Provisions relating to certain offences
verbatim_text: Whoever dishonestly commits breach of terms of finance, alienates or removes mortgaged property without permission of the financial institution shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and with fine.

title: Execution of decree
verbatim_text:
(1) Upon the grant of a decree, the decree shall be executed by the Banking Court as if it were a decree passed by a Civil Court under Order XXI CPC.
(2) All questions arising between the parties relating to execution, discharge or satisfaction shall be determined by the Banking Court.

title: Application of fines and costs
verbatim_text: The Banking Court may direct that any fine imposed under this Ordinance shall be applied in or towards the payment of the expenses of the prosecution or compensation to the financial institution.

title: Bar of jurisdiction
verbatim_text: No Court other than a Banking Court shall have or exercise any jurisdiction with respect to any matter to which the jurisdiction of a Banking Court extends under this Ordinance.

title: Appeal
verbatim_text:
(1) Any person aggrieved by any final judgment, decree or order of a Banking Court may, within thirty days of the date of the judgment, decree or order, prefer an appeal to the High Court.
(2) No appeal shall lie against an interlocutory order which does not dispose of the entire suit.
(6) No appeal shall be admitted for hearing unless the appellant deposits with the High Court an amount equivalent to the decretal amount or furnishes security as the Court may direct.

title: Restriction on transfer of properties
verbatim_text: From the date of receipt of notice under section 9, the defendant shall not transfer, alienate, encumber or part with possession of any property without the prior permission of the Banking Court.

title: Power to make rules
verbatim_text: The Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Ordinance.

title: Act to override other laws
verbatim_text: The provisions of this Ordinance shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force.

title: Removal of difficulties
verbatim_text: If any difficulty arises in giving effect to any of the provisions of this Ordinance, the Federal Government may make such order as appears to it to be necessary.

title: Finality of orders
verbatim_text: Subject to the provisions of section 22, no Court or authority shall call in question any order or decree passed by a Banking Court.

title: Indemnity
verbatim_text: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Federal Government, Banking Court, or financial institution for anything done in good faith under this Ordinance.

title: Repeal and savings
verbatim_text: (1) The Banking Companies (Recovery of Loans, Advances, Credits and Finances) Act, 1997 is hereby repealed.

title: Continuance of pending proceedings
verbatim_text: All proceedings pending before any Banking Court under the repealed enactment shall continue before the Banking Court established under this Ordinance.
